title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typed page ('- 21 -') is unrelated to the surrounding manuscript notes on motives, Deuring's element and adelic gerbes. It is the end of the proof of an analytic implicit function theorem (a 'Th. 1') for convergent power series over a valued field K. The proof uses Cauchy's method of majorants, in Bourbaki style: it cites '§1, th. 2' (substitution theorem), '§1, prop. 8' and 'Fonct. var. réelle, chap. V, §2'. It is most likely a Bourbaki draft on analytic functions or analytic varieties that ended up in this folder.

1. Existence. The proof reduces to finding q majorant power series v_k in t_1..t_p, absolutely summable and without constant term, solving (9): v_k = M/((1-μΣt_j)(1-μΣv_i)) - M - MμΣv_i.
2. The right side of (9) does not depend on k, so all v_k equal a common v. Put T=Σt_j and multiply by (1-qμv); this gives (10): (1-qμv)(1+qMμ)v = M/(1-μT) - M(1-qμv).
3. Expanding (10) gives a quadratic: v - qμ(1+qMμ)v² = M(1/(1-μT) - 1). The root vanishing at t=0 is v = [1 - sqrt(1 - 4Mqμ(1+qMμ)(1/(1-μT) - 1))] / (2qμ(1+qMμ)).
4. The binomial series for the square root, combined with the substitution theorem, shows that v is an absolutely summable power series without constant term on a polycylinder about 0. So majorants exist, and hence the formal solution u_i converges.
5. Uniqueness. Let w_i be continuous solutions of the fixed-point equations (11), vanishing at 0. Proposition 8 of §1 gives u_i - w_i = o(sup_k |u_k - w_k|) near 0, which forces u_i = w_i near 0.

This is the standard proof of the analytic implicit function theorem.
errors: The text states that (1-w)^{1/2} equals the sum of Σ binom(1/2,n) w^n. In fact Σ binom(1/2,n) w^n = (1+w)^{1/2}, and (1-w)^{1/2} = Σ binom(1/2,n)(-w)^n. This is a harmless sign slip; convergence for |w|<1 is unaffected.
The phrase 'on déduit aussitôt de (9) que si ce système a une solution, tous les v_i sont égaux' is trivially true, since the right-hand side does not depend on k. There is no gap.
The algebra from (9) to (10) and the closed formula for v check out correctly.

ideas.what: Existence of analytic solutions of implicit equations via an explicit majorant system solved by a square root
ideas.modern_name: Cauchy method of majorants; analytic implicit function theorem over a complete valued field
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (majorants); Weierstrass; standard textbook material (e.g. Serre, Lie Algebras and Lie Groups, Part II)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats (statement only); Serre LALG Part II, Ch. II

ideas.what: Uniqueness of continuous solutions via u-w = o(sup|u-w|)
ideas.modern_name: Local uniqueness for fixed-point equations with vanishing linear part (contraction-type argument)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Fonctions d'une variable réelle, ch. V (comparison of functions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine typed page proving the analytic implicit function theorem by majorants, apparently a Bourbaki-style draft misfiled among the motives notes. Its only historical interest is as evidence of Grothendieck's involvement in Bourbaki drafting, if it is indeed his. It contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed (tapuscrit), not manuscript, and belongs to a different text: a Bourbaki-style draft on power series and analytic functions. It is not part of the motives notes on the neighbouring pages.
'on déduit aussitôt que (9)' is corrected by hand to 'de (9)'; the transcription handles this correctly.
The binomial series is written in the original as Σ_{n=0}^∞ binom(1/2, n) w^n. The image matches the transcription; the mathematical sign slip is the author's, not a transcription error.
The marginal annotation '41' at the bottom left is probably an archival or folio number and was omitted by the transcription.
